name: com.sendfinery/spf-dkim-dmarc-checker
title: Sendfinery
description: Check a domain's SPF, DKIM, DMARC and MX records, look up DNS and read email headers. Web, API, MCP.

tools.name: check_spf
tools.description:
Check a domain's SPF record, the DNS TXT record (starting with v=spf1)
that lists the servers allowed to send email for the domain.

It checks that the domain has exactly one SPF record, parses it,
follows every include: and redirect= into a tree, and counts the DNS
lookups a receiver makes against RFC 7208's limit of 10 and the void
lookups (lookups that find nothing) against the limit of 2. Above
either limit receivers fail SPF for every message. It also flags +all
(any server may send as the domain), ?all, a missing all, ptr,
syntax errors and include loops.

Returns {"domain", "record" (the record text, null without exactly
one), "tree" (each node: domain, via, status, record, children),
"lookups", "lookups_exact" (false when counting stopped past the
limit, so lookups is a lower bound), "void_lookups", "findings"
(each {"level": "ok"|"info"|"warn"|"error", "code", "text"}; "info"
is a note that grades nothing), "grade" (the worst level)}. Show the
user the findings' text.

Credits: 1 per call.

domain.description: The domain to check, such as example.com. A URL or an email address works too: the tool takes the domain from it.

tools.name: check_dkim
tools.description:
Look up a domain's DKIM public keys in DNS and check them.

With a selector, reads the key at <selector>._domainkey.<domain>.
Without one, tries a fixed list of common selectors (Google Workspace,
Microsoft 365, Amazon SES, SendGrid, Mailchimp and others); DNS cannot
list a domain's selectors, so a key under any other name is not found
and `common_only` is true. If nothing is found, ask the user for the
s= tag of the DKIM-Signature header in a message they sent, and check
again with that selector.

Returns `found` (each selector with its DNS `name` and parsed `key`:
type `k`, RSA size `bits`, `testing`, `revoked`), `tried` (the
selectors queried), `findings` (level, code, text) and `grade`, the
worst level among the findings.

Credits: 1 per call.

domain.description: The domain that sends the mail, such as example.com.

selector.description: The DKIM selector: the s= tag of the DKIM-Signature header in a message the domain sent. Leave it out to try common selectors.

tools.name: check_dmarc
tools.description:
Look up the DMARC policy that applies to a domain and check it against RFC 9989
(which replaced RFC 7489 in 2026).

Use it when a user asks whether a domain has DMARC, why its mail fails DMARC or
lands in spam, or whether its DMARC reports arrive. When the domain has no record of
its own, the parent domains are tried (RFC 9989's DNS tree walk): `policy_domain`
names where the record was found and `inherited` says whether it is a parent's.
`effective_policy` is what receivers apply (none, quarantine or reject), `record`
holds the parsed tags, and `rua` says for each report address on another domain
whether that domain authorizes the reports. `findings` lists each problem in plain
English with what to change; `grade` is the worst level (ok, warn or error).

Credits: 1 per call.

domain.description: The domain to check, such as example.com. A URL or an email address works too: only its domain is used.

tools.name: lookup_mx
tools.description:
Look up where a domain receives email: its MX records, sorted by
preference, and the IPv4/IPv6 addresses of each mail server.

Use it to answer "which mail provider does this domain use", "why does
mail to this domain bounce" or "is this domain's MX set up right".
The result is `{"domain", "hosts": [{"preference", "host",
"addresses", "cname"}], "null_mx", "fallback", "findings": [{"level",
"code", "text"}], "grade"}`. `null_mx` true means the domain says it
receives no mail (RFC 7505). An empty `hosts` with a non-empty
`fallback` means the domain has no MX record and senders deliver to
those addresses instead. Relay the `findings` texts to the user: they
say what is wrong and what to change.

Credits: 1 per call.

domain.description: The domain, such as example.com. A URL or an email address works too: only its domain is used.

tools.name: lookup_dns
tools.description:
Look up a domain's DNS records through public resolvers (Quad9,
then Cloudflare), with no cache, so the answer is what the internet
sees now.

Returns `answers`, one per record type: `status` (ok, nxdomain for a
domain that does not exist, nodata for no record of that type,
timeout or error with a `reason`), `records` as text (MX as
"preference host", SOA as "mname rname serial refresh retry expire
minimum", CAA as 'flags tag "value"') and `ttl` in seconds. A CNAME
is followed for the other types, so their records can belong to the
name it points to. `findings` names a domain that does not exist and
queries that failed, and `grade` is the worst level among them.

Credits: 1 per call.

domain.description: The domain to look up, such as example.com.

types.description: Record types to look up: any of A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, CNAME, SOA and CAA. Leave it out to look up all eight.

tools.name: analyze_email_headers
tools.description:
Read an email's header and report how the message was delivered.

Headers are parsed in memory and not stored. Nothing is looked up in
DNS: the verdicts are the ones the receiving server wrote.

Returns `subject`, `date` and `message_id`; `from_domain`,
`return_path_domain` and `dkim_domains`; `hops` (the Received headers
oldest first: `from_host`, `by_host`, `with_protocol`, `timestamp` and
`delay_seconds` since the previous hop); `authserv_id` and
`auth_results` (the SPF, DKIM and DMARC verdicts of the topmost
Authentication-Results header); `alignment` (`spf_aligned`,
`dkim_aligned`: whether the From domain matches the Return-Path and a
DKIM signature's d= domain; DMARC needs one); `findings` (level,
code, text) and `grade`, the worst level among the findings.

Credits: 1 per call.

headers.description: The message header as text, from the first Received: line down to the blank line before the body (a mail program's 'Show original' or 'View message source'). A whole message is fine; the body is ignored. At most 200 KB.

tools.name: check_domain
tools.description:
Check a domain's SPF, DMARC, DKIM and MX records at once.

One call runs four checks and costs 3 checks. DKIM tries only a fixed
list of common selectors (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Amazon SES,
SendGrid, Mailchimp and others), since DNS cannot list a domain's
selectors; for a key under another name, use check_dkim with the s=
tag of the DKIM-Signature header in a message the domain sent.

Returns `spf`, `dmarc`, `dkim` and `mx`, each with its own `findings`
(level, code, text) and `grade`, and the overall `grade`: the worst
level among all findings (ok, warn or error).

Credits: 3 per call.

domain.description: The domain to check, such as example.com.

tools.name: list_watched_domains
tools.description:
List the domains your account watches, oldest first.

Each domain has its latest `grade` (ok, warn or error; null before its
first check), `last_checked_at` and `next_check_at` (every 7 days),
and `paused`: a domain past your plan's limit, kept but not checked.
Also returns `limit` (how many domains your plan watches: free 1,
Essential 10, Scale 50; null for no limit) and `used`. Requires an
account (an API key or sign-in).

Credits: free. This tool is not metered.

tools.name: watch_domain
tools.description:
Start watching a domain: Sendfinery checks its SPF, DMARC, DKIM
(common selectors) and MX now and again every 7 days, and sums up
the DMARC aggregate reports that arrive for it.

Returns the domain's report after its first check: `domain`, the
`findings` (section, level, code, text), the check in `checks`, and
empty DMARC totals in `week` and `month`. Refused with
`already_watched` when you watch it already, and with
`quota_exceeded` when your plan's domain limit is reached (free 1,
Essential 10, Scale 50). Requires an account (an API key or sign-in).

Credits: free. This tool is not metered.

domain.description: The domain, such as example.com. A URL or an email address works too.

tools.name: get_domain_report
tools.description:
Get the report of a domain you watch, from its stored checks and
DMARC reports (it runs no new check).

Returns `domain` (grade, last and next check, paused), `findings` of
the latest check (section spf, dkim, dmarc or mx; level ok, info (a
note that grades nothing), warn or error; code; text), `snapshot`
(the records the latest check read), `checks` (the last 10, newest
first, each with `changes`: what changed since the check before, in
words), and `week` and `month`: the DMARC
aggregate reports of the last 7 and 30 days, with `messages`,
`passed`, `pass_rate` (aligned DKIM or SPF) and `failing_sources`
(sending IPs that passed neither). Requires an account (an API key or
sign-in).

Credits: free. This tool is not metered.

domain.description: The domain, such as example.com. A URL or an email address works too.

tools.name: unwatch_domain
tools.description:
Stop watching a domain. Its check history and DMARC reports are
deleted and cannot be restored; watching it again starts afresh.
Returns the removed domain's name. Requires an account (an API key or
sign-in).

Credits: free. This tool is not metered.

domain.description: The domain, such as example.com. A URL or an email address works too.
